Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old woman with acute left-sided occipital headache since yesterday, no prior similar history, minimal relief with ibuprofen, no associated red flag symptoms.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache.
- Onset: Began mid-morning yesterday (1 day ago).
- Location: Left side at the back of the head (occipital).
- Nature: Intense, throbbing, gradual buildup over a short period of time.
- Severity: 8/10.
- Duration/progression: Persisting since onset, no specific worsening or improvement noted, no variation with time of day.
- Exacerbating/Relieving factors: No effect with changes in position (lying down, standing up, bending, coughing, sneezing). Minimal to no relief with ibuprofen (Nurofen).
- Associated symptoms:
  - No nausea, vomiting.
  - No tingling, numbness, or weakness.
  - No blurred vision, eye pain, photophobia, or visual disturbances.
  - No fever, shivering, sweating, or rash.
  - Normal appetite and fluid intake.
- Previous similar episodes: None; new symptom for patient.
- Impact: Finding it difficult to do work and normal activities; has not missed work yet.
- No reported triggers (lifestyle, stress, dietary changes).

Past Medical History:
- No known medical conditions.
- No stomach problems or asthma reported.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen (Nurofen), dose/route/frequency not documented, taken yesterday – minimal effect.
- No regular prescribed or over-the-counter medications.
- No documented allergies.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Designer.
- Non-smoker.
- Does not drink alcohol.
- Denies any other drug use.

Family History:
- Mother has hypertension.
- Mother also has migraines.

Physical Examination:
- No examination findings or vital signs documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results mentioned.
- Blood pressure has not been checked recently.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute new-onset unilateral occipital headache
  - Assessment: Concerning for a primary headache disorder; no red flag features elicited on history. No prior history of headache. No evidence of neurological deficit or systemic symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Recommend trial of stronger pain relief (alternative to ibuprofen, exact medication not specified), to be taken regularly with food (not to be used at the same time as ibuprofen).
    - Paracetamol recommended as adjunct.
    - Ensure rest and adequate hydration.
    - Advise to monitor for red flags: worsening pain, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, recurrent episodes, or new symptoms – instructed to seek prompt reassessment if these occur.
    - Follow-up: If not improving or worsening over the next day or two, or if any new concerning symptoms appear, patient instructed to call back for reassessment. Medication prescription to be provided from pharmacy.

General Plan items:
- None additional.

● Missing but clinically expected elements: 
  - No physical exam or neurological assessment performed/reported.
  - No vital signs recorded.
  - Medication dosing, route, frequency not specified.
  - Allergies: negative confirmed.
  - No direct fundoscopic or meningeal assessment documented.
● No internal conflicts noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear, no significant noise or inaudible sections.
